extracted.intended_audience: participants and stakeholders in antidumping administrative reviews (exporters, importers, counsel, U.S. Department of Commerce staff, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection)
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice announcing a court decision not in harmony with Commerce's final results in an antidumping administrative review and explaining Commerce's amended final results, cash-deposit instructions, liquidation/assessment treatment, and legal bases (Timken requirements and statutory citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timken publication and suspension requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When a court decision is not 'in harmony' with a Commerce determination, Commerce must publish a notice of that court decision and suspend liquidation of entries pending a 'conclusive' court decision (Timken; as clarified by Diamond Sawblades).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice is published to satisfy the Timken publication requirement. The CIT's judgment constitutes a final decision not in harmony with Commerce's Final Results; therefore publication and suspension of liquidation are required pursuant to section 516A(c) and (e) of the Tariff Act and related case law (Timken Co. v. United States, 893 F.2d 337 (Fed. Cir. 1990); Diamond Sawblades Manufacturers Coalition v. United States, 626 F.3d 1374 (Fed. Cir. 2010)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of final results following a final court judgment not in harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is a final court judgment not in harmony with Commerce's final results, Commerce amends its Final Results with respect to the affected exporter(s) (e.g., revising the weighted-average dumping margin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the CIT issued a final judgment sustaining Commerce's third remand redetermination, Commerce amended the Final Results to change Jiangsu Senmao's weighted-average dumping margin to 14.35 percent. Publication of the amended final results fulfills the Timken notice requirement under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash deposit instruction rule when superseding rate exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If an exporter has a superseding cash deposit rate (i.e., final results were published in a subsequent administrative review), Commerce will not issue revised cash deposit instructions to CBP and the notice will not affect the current cash deposit rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Jiangsu Senmao has a superseding cash deposit rate from a subsequent review, Commerce will not change CBP cash-deposit instructions despite amending the prior Final Results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidation and injunction treatment pending appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries covered by a court order remain enjoined from liquidation pursuant to the terms of the injunction during the pendency of any appeals process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce remains enjoined by the CIT from liquidating entries exported by the subject exporter for the covered period; these entries will remain enjoined while appeals are pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment instruction following final court decision (19 CFR 351.212(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the court's ruling is not appealed, or if appealed and upheld by a final and conclusive decision, Commerce intends to instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on unliquidated entries in accordance with 19 CFR 351.212(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce will direct CBP to assess duties on appropriate entries covered by the review when the importer-specific ad valorem assessment rate is not zero or de minimis; where the importer-specific rate is zero or de minimis, Commerce will instruct CBP to liquidate without regard to antidumping duties (see 19 CFR 351.106(c)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Importer-specific ad valorem assessment and de minimis rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce will assess antidumping duties on appropriate entries when the importer-specific ad valorem assessment rate is not zero or de minimis; if the importer-specific rate is zero or de minimis, those entries will be liquidated without regard to antidumping duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment or liquidation decisions follow the importer-specific ad valorem rate outcome; citation to 19 CFR 351.106(c)(2) is provided for the de minimis/zero rate treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best available information standard for surrogate value selection
rubrics_metrics.description: In selecting surrogate inputs/data (for non-market economy antidumping calculations), Commerce must consider the 'best available information' and articulate why the chosen surrogate data are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CIT sustained Commerce's articulation that it considered the best available information and that use of two separate countries' surrogate value (SV) data was justified here. Commerce must explain its analysis and why selected SVs constitute the best available information when determining surrogate inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need to support surrogate country selection and adjustments with substantial evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Selections of surrogate country data and any adjustments to surrogate values must be supported by substantial evidence on the record; failure to do so can result in remand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CIT remanded prior Commerce determinations where Commerce failed to provide substantial evidence for departures from primary surrogate country practice, for selecting multiple SVs without justification, or for failing to include on the record documents relied upon to adjust SVs. Commerce's remand redeterminations must provide record evidence and explanations supporting SV choices and adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record inclusion requirement for documents relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce must place on the administrative record the documents it relied on to make adjustments to surrogate values or other determinations so the court and parties can review the basis for the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior remand was ordered because Commerce 'failed to include on the record the document which it relied on to adjust the Brazilian plywood SVs.' Commerce remedied this in subsequent remand redeterminations by providing the requested documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand/redetermination process obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: When the CIT remands Commerce's Final Results, Commerce must issue remand redeterminations addressing the court's findings, potentially multiple times until the court's concerns are resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The history in this case shows multiple remands (first, second, third) where Commerce reconsidered surrogate values, provided additional explanation and record evidence, and revised dumping margins accordingly. The remand process may require replacing data (e.g., replacing Brazilian plywood data with Malaysian data) and recalculating margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted-average dumping margin calculation using surrogate values
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce calculates weighted-average dumping margins using reported factors of production and surrogate values for certain inputs, selecting datasets (from surrogate countries) and making adjustments as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Final Results Commerce used Malaysian import data as SVs for certain logs, Brazilian data for other factors, and adjusted Brazilian import data for plywood after determining Spanish import data was erroneous; subsequent remands replaced some Brazilian data with Malaysian data and resulted in revised margins (from 39.27% to 14.35% for Jiangsu Senmao).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory publication authority and citation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices amending final results and announcing court decisions must cite the statutory authority under which they are issued (e.g., sections 516A(c) and (e) and 777(i)(1) of the Tariff Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice states it is issued and published in accordance with sections 516A(c) and (e) and 777(i)(1) of the Act, and provides case citations (Timken, Diamond Sawblades) and regulatory citations (19 CFR 351.212(b), 19 CFR 351.106(c)(2)) for assessment and liquidation treatments.
